review:
[i]Turok[/i] is a pretty fun, straightforward run-and-gun boomer shooter. It very much feels like a classic 90s FPS, for better and for worse, but if you’re into that style of game, it’s easy to recommend. It’s fast, simple, satisfying, and fun to explore. Just know going in that it still carries some old-school design quirks that might not be for everyone.

A lot of the fun for me came from simply moving through each level, exploring, finding keys, figuring out where to go next, and discovering secrets along the way. It has that older style of level design where progression is not always immediately obvious, and you’re expected to poke around, backtrack, and pay attention to the environment. That said, the same things that make it charming can also be dealbreakers for some people. There are missable items you may need for progression, secrets hidden in pretty obscure places, and some difficulty spikes late in the game that honestly feel kind of BS. The first few levels also feel a little same-y, though the game does introduce more variety as it goes on.

This re-release does an excellent job making the game more approachable. There are a lot of configuration options, including the ability to turn off the iconic head bobbing while walking or turning, which is great for anyone who gets motion sick. There are also some nice quality-of-life options you can mess with to make the experience smoother without completely losing the original feel.

This game aged really well, the art direction is great, the gunplay is fun, the enemy variety (especially in the latter half of the game) is great. The mix of platforming, shooting and puzzle solving is really well done and the overall flow and feel of the game is incredible.

What makes this extra bad is the way night dive decided to flag your saves if you use any cheats whatsoever, basically forcing you to replay the game if you didn't get all the secrets on 1st playthrough AND ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up your save files. Players shouldn't be able to fall into this kind of trap, even if it is their (my) own fault. Because this made me even more frustrated, I dug deep and found a workaround that I doubt night dive even cares about, but for anyone who cares/runs into the same issue, it is possible to get out of the final level without using in game cheats and flagging your save with disabled achievements.

Finally I finished Turok. I've been a fan of the series ever since I played the Xbox 360 one. Going back to the N64 trilogy and starting with the first, it feels oddly different. A lot of times when people talk about atmosphere, they bring up games like kings field, but I think Turok knocked it out of the park as well. 

The clouds give this weird dream like feeling to the areas and it's best captured in one of the areas where you're climbing a tree fortress, jumping through clouds, a giant brachiosaurus walks around you, shrouded by fog. You can only hear it's giant footsteps and the rumbling of thunder. It was awesome. One of my favourite FPS levels ever. I also enjoyed the later ones but from a challenging point of view.

However, that aside, some of these areas are absolutely cursed lol. In DOOM when you need to open a locked door, it clearly tells you what colored key you need. In Turok? You step on a stone pedestal and it unlocks SOMETHING. go figure out wtf it is. Most of times it's right there, but sometimes it's out of your way and I have no idea why the game does this lmao especially considering the game has a very Labyrinthian nature to it (which I both like and dislike at times). Otherwise the game is fairly linear, sometimes offering a choice between levels and the path being straightforward most of the time. 

But how does it feel as a shooter? Well pretty good. Its controls feel slightly jankier but there's no slidey movement so that's good. However, for some reason this game loves throwing platforming at you which I've never liked in an FPS. The guns are almost all cool, but some feel redundant (especially since they use the same ammo which I wasn't a fan of). Enemies range from alright (basic mobs) to pretty sick (dinosaurs with guns, hell yea). But ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, whichever genius decided it would be a good idea to respawn enemies casually, why??? The beam of light randomly summoning enemies was probably my least favourite aspect of the entire game.

Other than that, I had fun with it. The bosses were weird. You literally start with a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ jeep as your first boss lmao, and it only gets better from there. I'm not sure I enjoyed the final boss much especially considering it was right after the much, much superior T-Rex boss fight. 

Anyway, solid ambience, great atmosphere, mediocre shooting, fun enemy designs, good range of weapons. A solid 7/10. Good stuff and I'm looking forward to the rest of the trilogy

Released all the way back in 1997 on the N64, Turok is first-person shooter set in a strange world where you'll come across humans, dinosaurs and aliens alike. This version on Steam is not the first time the game was on PC, but compared to the original PC port and the console version, this port runs better, looks better and includes some QoL changes, like increased draw distance and better frame rate.

The game is reminicient of boomer shooters that came out before it, being light on the story and heavy on the action, along with gameplay mechanics like side strafing making you move faster than running forward. 
- You have eight levels you'll play through, finding keys for later levels in the earlier ones, ranging from jungles to catacombs. The levels can take up to around an hour or so to clear, give or take. It depends on how well you know them and how quickly you're trying to get through them.
- There are plenty of weapons to find and use, something that the sequel would improve upon.
- Great variety of enemies, altough the more outlandish enemy types don't show up until you're at the final levels of the game.

Positives include: 
- The well-made level design of the game, as the levels manage to be easy and fun to navigate despite the old graphics and tilesets that are often re-used. Most of them are straightforward and you'll often loop back to a spot you were at earlier as you collect a key, like a door that was locked earlier. Compared to the massive, labyrinithan levels of Turok 2, playing this game is arguably "easier" and more relaxing. There have been some small changes made to certain levels but they are minor and don't make the experience worse, but for any purists out there, you should know that there has been some tampering.

-The different guns that you can mess around with are fun to use, and you'll never run short of ammo unless you play on the highest difficulty, at which point you should run past most enemies. One of them is a weapon you can assemble by finding all the pieces scattared around different levels which will turn the final boss into a complete joke.

-Dinosaurs. Dinosaurs are always a positive.

Negatives include:
-Boss battles appear in some levels and while I like boss battles in games, in Turok, there are no unique mechanics to them. While they will do different attacks and such, the way to beat them is always the same. You just side strafe and run backwards while you unload every weapon you have on the boss untill it dies.
- Hardcore difficulty makes enemies into bullet sponges, while you also take more damage. This is nothing unusual, but in practice Hardcore becomes almost like a speedrun where you want to avoid all enemies that you don't have to kill, because engaging with then normally will leave you with no ammo and taking unnecessary damage.
- For a game called "Turok: Dinosaur Hunter": you'll be killing more humans, generic monsters and robots than prehistoric animals. What is in the game is alright, but I wish there was more dinosaur variety.

All in all, this is an excellent game and a very good PC port. If you liked Turok back then on the N64, you'll  like this port a lot. If you didn't like it back then due to the controls and certain limitations of the console, then I'd say give this one a shot, as the game is much smoother to play now. For anyone new to the series, if you like old-school FPS games then you should definitely give Turok a try.

What can be said of Turok: Dinosaur Hunter, a game that originally released in 1997 (for the Nintendo 64 no less), that hasn't been said numerous times already?

Not much, so I'll refrain from repeating the most obvious accolades that adorn this game. 

For those of you who are just discovering Turok for the first time, welcome, this is without a doubt the best way to experience this incredible title. For those of you who first stepped into the Lost Land using a funky, single analog stick and c-buttons for movement, welcome to a refreshingly smooth and silky, high definition version of Acclaim / Iguana's N64 debut title!

It cannot be overstated how good this game feels with true mouse & keyboard controls. It almost feels like cheating when you are swiftly moving through the corridors of the Campaigner's mothership, taking out robots, giant mechs, aliens, and sewer monsters like John Wick on steroids. And, at the same time, the modified gamepad support also feels amazing and quite fitting for a frustration-free, nostalgic trip back to the days of the original game.

This is important too, because Turok is just as much a platformer as it is an FPS. Tight jumps, thin ledges, ladders, beams, and vine-covered walls make up a large portion of the game. Indeed, the thing that set Turok apart when it released was this magic combination of action platforming done from the first-person perspective - sorry Thief and Metroid Prime, Turok beat you to the punch. 

Aside from the wonderful control, the entire game has been rebuilt in widescreen with much higher resolution graphics. Now, remember, this is a game that is three decades old, so a remake this is not. However, that is precisely what makes it so special. 

All of the fun cheats and exploits are still present, as is the awesome music and ambient sound effects which have undergone digital improvements to make them even clearer. You will also find a number of options that allow you to adjust the game to your preferred playstyle (some of these options have caused a bit of a rift in the Turok community, but I always say the more the merrier as long as the original experience remains intact.) 

Anyway, for me, Turok: Dinosaur Hunter remains my favorite of the original trilogy (Tal'Set FTW!). Nightdive Studios has delivered a beautiful package full of TLC and respect for the original game. I am so happy that a new generation of gamers gets to experience this classic title on modern hardware. It may not look like Doom the Dark Ages, but Turok is a blast to play. And isn't that why we love video games? To have fun?

Highly recommended to old and new fans alike!

The OG Nintendo 64 dinosaur boomer shooter TUROK is lovingly remastered in Nightdive's KEX engine, and it rules. Originally releasing only one year following 1996's Quake, TUROK is a game absolutely and 100% rooted in 1990's aesthetics, mechanics, and attitude. Gameplay is fast and ridiculous; you will take on bad guys, dinosaurs and aliens at a breakneck pace with a very amusing 14 weapon arsenal. 

Level design is fun and I do like it overall, but can become a little tedious, long, and samey-looking. If you are new to boomer shooter design, these levels could feel too annoying. There is a fair amount of platforming that can occasionally get frustratingly difficult, but is mostly done very well and adds plenty of tension and fun to traversing TUROK's world. 

TUROK looks, sounds and plays extremely well. This game is silly and fun.

A dinamica de procurar chaves e segredos nas fases é bem envolvente, o jogo contém boss fights bastante interessantes e divertidas, com o design dos monstros sendo bem legais, o level design das fases também é ótimo!! Realmente, um jogo bem a frente de seu tempo e no geral, extremamente divertido e viciante. Vale lembrar também que certas fases podem se estender até demais ou ficarem muito labirínticas.. fazendo se perder ficar fácil. Esse jogo também não tem muita lore em comparação aos outros da franquia, ele é mais direto ao ponto: índio fodão mata dinossauros e aliens com armas ainda mais fodas. Enfim, belissimo jogo, recomendo !!!
